newsitem.title: UK: Europe/US refining margins better, Asia still lead.
newsitem.headline: Europe/US refining margins better, Asia still lead.

text.p: Oil refineries' profit margins in Europe and the United States recovered last week from recent lows but remain depressed, according to Reuters price data using standard product yields.
But margins in Singapore are soaring, having gained about $3 a barrel over the past couple of months.
Although they fell back slightly last week, profits at complex refineries in Singapore averaged about $5.39 a barrel for Dubai crude, well above the profit levels of their Western counterparts.
In particular, gas oil has made big gains in recent weeks climbing to $9.27 a barrel above Dubai crude from about $4.70 at the start of February.
Gasoline also remains bouyant at over $10 a barrel above Dubai despite falling back from over $11 above a week ago.
Last week was mixed for refiners in Europe. Those based in Rotterdam averaged about $1.36 a barrel running Brent in a typical complex plant, ending the week at $1.19 after a late spike on wet Brent.
Despite the softer tone at the end of the week, margins remain well above the sub-$1 a barrel levels seen at the beginning of the month.
Longer term, profits have drifted steadily lower from a peak of $3.50 a barrel in October last year.
Much of the recent rise in profits has been due to gasoline which has consistently managed to outpace gains in Brent.
Gasoline stands nearly $5 a barrel above Brent compared to an average of $2.75 during the fourth quarter last year and a low point of under $2 at the beginning of January.
The recovery in profit margins at cracking refineries in Rotterdam has also been seen at less sophisticated hydroskimming plants.
They ended the week below breakeven but are above the 60 cents a barrel loss seen in the last days of February.
Mediterranean profit margins gained ground last week as the refinery maintenance season got under way, taking capacity temporarily off the market.
Complex refiners processing Urals made profits of about $1.47 a barrel last week, ending at $1.33.
Dealers said exports of Iraqi crude oil continued to help keep crude oil prices low but saw complex refiners continuing to reap much more reward than simple hydroskimming plant.
Last Friday, the United Nations approved a cut of 25 cents a barrel in the price of Iraqi crude which could exert further downward pressure on Urals.
Hydroskimming refineries have run at a loss for the past three months in the Mediterranean and have lagged the pick up in profits at their more complex competitors.
Last week they ended 40 cents a barrel below breakeven and some $1.73 less than protitable complex refiners.
In the U.S. Gulf, refiners ended last week making profits of $1.13 a barrel running Brent and 35 cents a barrel on West Texas Intermediate.
As in Europe this is well above lows hit at the start of the month but under the high levels seen last November.
--Sam Arnold-Forster, London newsroom 542 4984
